bounds: Equity means you own shares now, though the share class determines your rights.
A convertible note is usually a debt instrument that may convert into shares later.
It commonly has a principal amount, interest rate, maturity date, and conversion terms, but the actual document controls.
If a note does not convert, the company may owe repayment, yet an early-stage company can lack the cash to pay.
A SAFE is different: it is generally not debt and does not typically accrue interest or mature like a note.
For a simple illustration, a $1,000 note at 6% simple annual interest for one year would accrue $60 before any repayment or conversion, assuming its terms and timing work that way.
This is not a forecast of what an investor will receive.
Compare current ownership rights, repayment priority, maturity, conversion triggers, and what happens in a sale or shutdown.
Never assume all convertible instruments behave alike.
